issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting specifications for the type of Animal.name (the UML shows 'name: String' while the text explicitly instructs to use StringBuilder). The provided solution's Animal implementation uses a String for the name field, which does not follow the textual instruction. This inconsistency can confuse students about which type to use and which API (String vs. StringBuilder) their getters/setters/constructors should expose.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and implementation consistent. Either (A) update the problem statement UML and the textual instruction to both require a String for the Animal.name attribute, or (B) change the solution (and any template guidance) so Animal.name is a StringBuilder and update the constructor, getter, and setter to accept/return StringBuilder (or provide clear conversion behavior). Ensure the problem statement explicitly states which type students must implement to avoid ambiguity.

issues.description: The problem text instructs that the Animal.name attribute should use StringBuilder for efficient modifications, but the problem UML shows 'name: String' and the reference solution implements the attribute as a String (private String name). This creates a cross-artifact mismatch about the concrete representation of the same conceptual attribute (the animal's name) and may confuse students about the expected type and corresponding getter/setter behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification and implementation: either (a) update the problem statement and UML to require a String name (remove the StringBuilder recommendation) so the solution remains correct; or (b) update the reference solution and any template/boilerplate to implement the Animal.name attribute as a StringBuilder (e.g., private StringBuilder name; adjust constructor, getName()/setName() to work with StringBuilder or expose appropriate String-returning getters) and update the UML to show name: StringBuilder. Ensure all usages (getName(), constructors, and string concatenations) are adjusted accordingly so students can clearly map the requirement to the implementation.
